Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 111, verse 1–3:

Meccan; it has seventy-seven letters, twenty words, and five verses.

We were informed by al-Harathi, who said: Abu al-Shaykh al-Hafiz related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us, saying: Salam ibn Salim related to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umamah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the surah of Tabbat, I hope that Allah, glorified is He, will not gather him and Abu Lahab in one abode." [299] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/474.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he.﴾

We were informed by Abd Allah ibn Hamid, who said: Makki related to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Hashim related to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Numayr related to us, saying: al-A'mash related to us, from Abd Allah ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿And warn your closest kinsmen﴾ [[Surah al-Shu'ara': 214.]], the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went up to al-Safa, climbed upon it, and then called out: "Yaa sabahaah!" People gathered around him, some coming in person and others sending their messengers. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O sons of Abd al-Muttalib, O sons of Fihr, O sons of Adi, if I informed you that cavalry at the foot of this mountain intended to raid you, would you believe me?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment." [300] [[Tafsir al-Tabari, Jami' al-Bayan: 19/147; Sahih al-Bukhari: 3/190.]] Abu Lahab said: "Perish you all for the rest of this day! Did you call us only for this?" Then Allah revealed: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾, meaning: he has failed and lost; ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾, meaning: he perished.

He spoke of his hands while meaning himself, in keeping with the Arab practice of expressing the whole by a part, as in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿for what your hands have earned﴾ [[Surah al-Shura: 30.]], and ﴿what their hands have sent ahead﴾ [[Surah al-Baqarah: 95.]], and similar verses. It has also been said that "yad" (hand) is an added element (silah), as the Arabs say: "yad al-dahr" (the hand of time), "yad al-raza'ya" (the hand of calamities) and "yad al-manaya" (the hand of deaths). The poet said:

When the hand of calamities swooped down upon him, he called out: "Is there no protector?"

It has also been said that what is meant is his wealth and possessions; it is said: "So-and-so is poor in what is in his hand (qalil dhat al-yad)," meaning wealth.

Al-tabab means loss and destruction. I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habibi say: I heard Muhammad ibn Mas'ud al-Suri say: I heard Nifawayh say: I heard al-Minqari, from al-Asma'i, from Abu Amr ibn al-Ala', who said:

When Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) was killed, they heard the voice of a invisible caller from the jinn weeping:

They left you and departed, so they did not turn back nor return,
and they did not fulfill their vow, so woe to what they did.

[[In the source: "ababu" instead of "raja'u"; in the source: "fa-ya tabban lima" instead of "fa-tabban lilladhi".]] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/235.]]

Abu Lahab is the son of Abd al-Muttalib; his name was Abd al-Uzza, which is why he is not named here. It has also been said that his name was Kutayba. Muqatil said: he was given the kunya Abu Lahab because of his handsome appearance and the radiance of his face, as though his two cheeks blazed.

﴿And perish he﴾: the waw here is the waw of conjunction. Abd Allah (ibn Mas'ud) and Ubayy (ibn Ka'b) read "wa-qad tabba." The first (tabbat) is a supplication and the second is like saying "may Allah forgive you," and "He has indeed done it" and "Allah has destroyed him, and He has indeed done it." The waw here is the waw of circumstance (waw al-hal).

The common reading is ﴿Abi Lahab﴾ with a fatha on the ha', while the people of Mecca read it with a sukun. They did not differ over His saying ﴿dhata lahab﴾ (possessing a blaze), that its ha' is fathah, because they observed the rhythm of the verse endings (ru'us al-ayy).

We were informed by al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, who said: al-Sunni related to us, saying: Hamid ibn Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb al-Balkhi related to us, saying: Shurayh ibn Yunus related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Mansur informed us, from al-Hakam, from Abu Zabyan, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Allah created the pen, He said: "Write what is to occur." It wrote, among what it wrote: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾.

And Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us, saying: Abu al-Tayyib Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak al-Tha'iri informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ashras al-Sulami related to us, saying: Abd al-Samad ibn Hassan al-Marwarrudhi related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, who said: al-Hasan was asked about His saying ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab﴾: was it in the Mother of the Book, and could Abu Lahab have avoided entering the Fire? Al-Hasan said: "By Allah, he could not have avoided it, and it is in the Book of Allah before Abu Lahab and his parents were created." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 20/237.]]

What supports this is what

Abu Tahir ibn Khuzayma informed us, in Sha'ban of the year three hundred and eighty-four, saying: our grandfather, Imam al-A'imma Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzayma, informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Amr related to us, saying: Za'ida related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Adam and Musa disputed. Musa said: 'O Adam, you are the one whom Allah, glorified is He, created with His hand and breathed into you of His spirit; you misled the people and expelled them from the Garden.' Adam said: 'And you, Musa, are the one whom Allah chose for His speech; do you blame me for an action that He had written against me before He created the heavens and the earth?' He said: 'So Adam overcame Musa in argument.'" [301] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/398.]]

And Muhammad ibn al-Fadl informed us, saying: our grandfather informed us, saying: I was present at the assembly of Ishaq ibn Ibrahim while I was on the reins of the riding animals, and he read to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, saying: Hammad ibn Salama related to us, from Ammar ibn Abi Ammar, client of Banu Hashim, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Musa met Adam and said: 'You are Adam, whom Allah created with His hand, had His angels prostrate to you, and settled in His Garden; you expelled your offspring from the Garden.' He said to him: 'O Musa, you are the one whom He chose with His message and His speech; so do I precede the Remembrance (al-dhikr)?' He said: 'The Remembrance.' So Adam overcame Musa, so Adam overcame Musa." [302] [[Musnad Ibn Rahawayh: 1/172; Musnad Ibn al-Ja'd: 164, with variation.]]

And Muhammad ibn al-Fadl informed us, saying: our grandfather informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, saying: Abu al-Zinad related to us, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Adam and Musa disputed. Musa said: 'O Adam, you are our father; you disappointed us and expelled us from the Garden.' Adam said: 'O Musa, Allah chose you with His speech and inscribed for you with His hand; do you blame me for a matter that Allah, exalted is He, decreed before He created me by forty years?' So Adam overcame Musa, so Adam overcame Musa." [303] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 7/214.]]

﴿What his wealth availed him, nor what he earned.﴾

Ibn Mas'ud said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) invited his kinsmen to Allah, glorified is He, Abu Lahab said to his companions: "If what my nephew says is true, then I will ransom myself, my property and my children." So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿What availed﴾, meaning: what avails. It has also been said: meaning, what thing availed him, his wealth, against the punishment of Allah.

Abu al-Aliyah said: "It means his flocks; he was the owner of herds and livestock." ﴿And what he earned﴾: meaning his children.

Al-A'mash read "wa-ma iktasaba" and related it from Ibn Mas'ud.

We were informed by al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, who said: Ahmad ibn Hanbal related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: "I was with Ibn Abbas one day when the sons of Abu Lahab came, disputing over something between them; they fought in his presence in the house. He stood to separate them, but one of them pushed him and he fell onto the couch. Ibn Abbas became angry and said: 'Get the wicked earnings out of my sight' — meaning his children, that they are earnings." [[Mustadrak al-Sahihayn: 2/539; Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq: 3/406.]]

The evidence for this interpretation is what

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me [...] [[A blank in the photographed manuscript.]].

Abu Hamza said: Imarah ibn Umayr al-Tamimi related to me, from his paternal aunt Sawda, who said: She said to Aisha: "I eat from the property of my child." Aisha said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The best of what one of you eats is from his earnings, and his child is from his earnings.'" [304] [[Kanz al-Ummal: 4/9, no. 9233.]] [[In the source "al-rajul" instead of "ahadukum".]]

﴿He will enter a Fire of blazing flame.﴾ The sin in "sayasla" is the sin of "sawfa," and it has been said it is the sin of promise.

The common reading has a fatha on the first ya' (yasla), while Abu Raja' read it with a damma, and Shuhayb al-Uqayli read it with a damma and a shadda on the lam.

﴿A Fire of blazing flame.﴾

Adam said: 'And you, Musa, are the one whom Allah chose for His speech; do you blame me for an action that He had written against me before He created the heavens and the earth?' He said: 'So Adam overcame Musa in argument.'" [301] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/398.]]

And Muhammad ibn al-Fadl informed us, saying: our grandfather informed us, saying: I was present at the assembly of Ishaq ibn Ibrahim while I was on the reins of the riding animals, and he read to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, saying: Hammad ibn Salama related to us, from Ammar ibn Abi Ammar, client of Banu Hashim, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Musa met Adam and said: 'You are Adam, whom Allah created with His hand, had His angels prostrate to you, and settled in His Garden; you expelled your offspring from the Garden.' He said to him: 'O Musa, you are the one whom He chose with His message and His speech; so do I precede the Remembrance (al-dhikr)?' He said: 'The Remembrance.' So Adam overcame Musa, so Adam overcame Musa." [302] [[Musnad Ibn Rahawayh: 1/172; Musnad Ibn al-Ja'd: 164, with variation.]]

And Muhammad ibn al-Fadl informed us, saying: our grandfather informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, saying: Abu al-Zinad related to us, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Adam and Musa disputed. Musa said: 'O Adam, you are our father; you disappointed us and expelled us from the Garden.' Adam said: 'O Musa, Allah chose you with His speech and inscribed for you with His hand; do you blame me for a matter that Allah, exalted is He, decreed before He created me by forty years?' So Adam overcame Musa, so Adam overcame Musa." [303] [[Sahih al-Bukhari: 7/214.]]

﴿What his wealth availed him, nor what he earned.﴾

Ibn Mas'ud said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) invited his kinsmen to Allah, glorified is He, Abu Lahab said to his companions: "If what my nephew says is true, then I will ransom myself, my property and my children." So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿What availed﴾, meaning: what avails. It has also been said: meaning, what thing availed him, his wealth, against the punishment of Allah.

Abu al-Aliyah said: "It means his flocks; he was the owner of herds and livestock." ﴿And what he earned﴾: meaning his children.

Al-A'mash read "wa-ma iktasaba" and related it from Ibn Mas'ud.

We were informed by al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, who said: Ahmad ibn Hanbal related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: "I was with Ibn Abbas one day when the sons of Abu Lahab came, disputing over something between them; they fought in his presence in the house. He stood to separate them, but one of them pushed him and he fell onto the couch. Ibn Abbas became angry and said: 'Get the wicked earnings out of my sight' — meaning his children, that they are earnings." [[Mustadrak al-Sahihayn: 2/539; Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq: 3/406.]]

The evidence for this interpretation is what

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me [...] [[A blank in the photographed manuscript.]].

Abu Hamza said: Imarah ibn Umayr al-Tamimi related to me, from his paternal aunt Sawda, who said: She said to Aisha: "I eat from the property of my child." Aisha said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The best of what one of you eats is from his earnings, and his child is from his earnings.'" [304] [[Kanz al-Ummal: 4/9, no. 9233.]] [[In the source "al-rajul" instead of "ahadukum".]]

﴿He will enter a Fire of blazing flame.﴾ The sin in "sayasla" is the sin of "sawfa," and it has been said it is the sin of promise.

The common reading has a fatha on the first ya' (yasla), while Abu Raja' read it with a damma, and Shuhayb al-Uqayli read it with a damma and a shadda on the lam.

﴿A Fire of blazing flame.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 111, verses 4–5:

And his wife, Umm Jamil bint Harb ibn Umayya, the sister of Abu Sufyan, and she was ʿawraʾ (one-eyed/blind in one eye, or having a defect in her eye). ﴿The carrier of firewood﴾. It is said: the talk and the lies. Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Qatada and al-Suddi said: she used to walk about with tale-bearing (namimah). The Arabs say: "So-and-so incites (yahtibu) against so-and-so" when he stirs up strife (tawrasha) and incites (aghza) between them. Their poet said:

"Of the fair ones, one who has not been hunted on the back of a mare, and who has not walked among the tribe with dry firewood (al-hatab al-rutab)."

That is, he did not walk about with tale-bearing (al-namaʾim). Another said:

"We are not like one who hopes for his speech to be halved, who scatters the rebellious dry wood and the dried-up thicket (al-ghayl al-yabs)."

[Note in the manuscript: as it stands in the manuscript.]

Mamar narrated from Qatada, who said: she used to reproach the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for poverty, and she used to gather firewood, and was reproached for that. This is a weak opinion, because Allah, glorified is He, described them as possessing wealth and children, and carrying firewood is not a fault. Al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: she used to bring thorns and thistles and throw them at night on the path of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in order to injure him; this is also the narration of ʿAtiyya from Ibn ʿAbbas. Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas said: she used to spread saʿdan (a thorny plant) on the path of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he would tread on it as one treads on silk and brocade.

Murra al-Hamdani: Umm Jamil used to come every day with a bundle of hasak (thorny prickly plant) and throw it on the path of the Muslims. One day, while she was carrying a bundle, she became tired and sat down on a stone to rest. An angel came to her from behind and struck her, and she perished.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "the carrier of sins." His evidence is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿and they bear their burdens upon their backs﴾ [al-Anʿam: 31], and the saying of the Arabs: "So-and-so carries wood on his back" when he does evil; "So-and-so is a carrier of firewood against his people" when he is the perpetrator among them; and "So-and-so is one against whom firewood is carried" when he is the one wronged.

The reading of the majority is with the nominative (raf') in both words, and Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim chose it. It has two possible readings: first, ﴿he will burn in a fire, he and his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾; second, ﴿and his wife, the carrier of firewood, [will be] in the fire as well﴾.

The argument of those who read with raf' is what Muhammad ibn Nuʿaym told us, who said: al-Husayn ibn Ayyub told us, who said: ʿAli ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz told us, who said: Abu ʿUbayd told us, who said: Hajjaj ibn Harun told us, who said: In the reading of ʿAbdullah (ibn Masʿud): "and his wife, carrier of firewood (ḥammālatun lil-ḥaṭab)."

Al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ibn Muhtadir, al-Aʿraj and ʿAsim read ḥammālata with the accusative (naṣb), and it has two possible readings: first, as a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl) and as a qaṭʿ (detached epithet), because its original form is "and his wife, the carrier of the firewood"; when the alif and lam were removed, the expression took the accusative. Second, it is an accusative of blame and abuse, like His saying: ﴿cursed﴾ [al-Ahzab: 61].

Ibn Abi al-Ziyad narrated from his father, who said: most of the Arabs used to read ḥammālata al-ḥaṭab; and Abu Qilaba read "wa-imra'atuhu ḥammālatu al-ḥaṭab" in the nominative as the agent (fāʿil). Al-ḥaṭab is a collective noun whose singular is ḥaṭaba.

Some of the linguists said: al-ḥaṭab here is the plural of al-ḥāṭib, who is the guilty party; meaning, she used to bring them to enmity through tale-bearing. Its parallels in speech are: rāṣid and rasad, ḥāris and ḥaras, ṭālib and ṭalab, ghāʾib and ghayb. The reason for likening tale-bearing to firewood is that firewood is kindled and ignited, and so is tale-bearing. Aktham ibn Sayfi said to his sons: "Beware of tale-bearing, for it is a burning fire, and the tale-bearer works in one hour what the sorcerer does not work in a month." A poet took it and said:

"Tale-bearing is a fire, woe, burning; so flee from it and keep away from whoever engages in it."

That is why it is said: the fire of resentment does not die down.

The second reason: firewood becomes fire, and fire is the cause of separation; so too is tale-bearing. Abu al-Qasim [al-Habibi] recited to me, saying: Abu Muhammad al-Harani al-Juwayni recited to me:

"Indeed the sons of al-Adram are carriers of firewood; they are the slanderers in contentment and in anger."

"Upon them is curse after curse, and war."

﴿Around her neck (fi jidiha)﴾: her neck. Dhu al-Rumma said:

"Your eye is her eye, your color is her color, and your neck is hers, except that she is not unadorned."

Its plural is ajyad. Al-Aʿsha said:

"And a desert whose mounds look like men of Iyad at its necks."

﴿A rope of fiber (masad)﴾: scholars differed about it. Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr said: a chain of iron, its length seventy cubits; it enters from its mouth and exits from its back, and the rest is wound around her neck. Al-Suddi said: it is the chain of iron that turns in Hell as a rope and bucket turn in a well. Al-Aʿmash narrated from Mujahid: of iron. Mansur narrated from him: al-masad is the iron piece that is in the pulley, called the axle (al-mihwar); this is the view of ʿAta' and ʿIkrima. Al-Shaʿbi and Muqatil: of palm fiber (layf). Al-Dahhak and others: in this world it was of palm fiber, the rope with which she used to gather firewood, and Allah, exalted is He, choked her with it and destroyed her; and in the Hereafter, of fire. Qatada: a necklace of rudaʿ (a kind of fiber). Al-Hasan: it was only beads on her neck. Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab: she had a splendid necklace around her neck, and she said: "I will spend it in enmity to Muhammad." Ibn Zayd: ropes of a tree that grows in Yemen called al-masad, and it used to be twisted. Al-Murruj (of the sacred month) and al-silm (the peace) and al-masad in the speech of the Arabs: every rope, whatever its material is changed, whether of palm fiber or other; its origin is from al-masad, which is twisting. A mamsuda creature is one of strong build when it is firmly bound. The poet said:

"A masad, bitter, of she-camels, not with fangs nor with canines."

Its plural is amsad. Al-Aʿsha said:

"She evening, and its door is shut behind us, a lock whose bolt rattles, of the twisted ones (amsad)."

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Nisaburi say: I heard Abu Nasr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Mulajjan al-Basri say: I heard Bishr ibn Musa al-Asadi say: I heard al-Asmaʿi say: Four poets prayed behind an imam named Yahya, and he recited ﴿Say: He is Allah, One﴾, and he stumbled in it. One of them said:

"Yahya has made many errors in 'Say: He is Allah, One.'"

The second said:

"He stood a long time, silent, until when he was exhausted he prostrated."

The third said:

"He groans in his prayer niche, like the groan of a pregnant woman for her child."

The fourth said:

"As if his tongue were bound with a rope of masad."

In this surah there is clear evidence of the prophethood of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). Allah, glorified is He, informed of the destiny of Abu Lahab and his wife to the Fire, and they were among the most eager of people to deny the Prophet (ﷺ). Yet this did not lead them to show faith in order to deny the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); rather they persisted in their disbelief, until it became known that Allah's threat against them and His report of their destiny to the Fire is true and sincere.
